title: COMPLICATIONS DURING DRILLING  OF ALUMINOSILICATE ROCKS, INCLUDING RESERVOIRS  WITH HARD-TO-RECOVER RESERVES
abstract: <jats:p>The walls of deep wells under construction in the southern Siberian platform consist of almost 30 % various aluminosilicates, the complex anions of which contain silicon and aluminum. Drilling such rocks poses a high risk of complications. Allaluminosilicates are capable of absorbing water and swelling to varying degrees. The swelling of clay minerals is based on adsorption, osmotic, and capillary forces. Swelling of substances is determined by the mass amount of absorbed liquid, the increase in the volume of the original substance, the amount of heat released during swelling, and other methods. Swelling of clay rocks results in their softening, collapse of the borehole walls of wells under construction, and deterioration of the reservoir properties. Both field and laboratory studies were conducted to select the optimal formulations and properties of drilling fluids for drilling into clay deposits in productive and unproductive formations. The significant amount of cementing material in the productive terrigenous deposits of the southern Angara-Lena steppe, composed of layered aluminosilicates, results in relatively poor reservoir properties and a high residual water saturation coefficient. Under these initial conditions, even a small amount of additional aqueous phase penetrating the formation disrupts the existing equilibrium and reduces rock permeability if the physicochemical properties of the drilling fluid filtrate are inadequate for the formation conditions. Numerous field and laboratory data indicate that drilling fluid components are involved in disrupting the wellbore-formation hydrodynamic connection and reducing the permeability of the near-wellbore formation zone by 40–60 % relative to its natural value. Sodium chloride brine-based drilling fluid, used for many years in exploration work in the southern Siberian Platform, has significantly compromised deep drilling results, obscuring the true productivity of the areas explored. Currently, it is necessary to introduce alternative drilling fluid systems for the opening of clay rocks in oil, gas and industrial brine fields in the south of the Siberian platform.</jats:p>
